newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco-Tunisia look to harmonising policies.
newsitem.headline: Morocco-Tunisia look to harmonising policies.

text.p: Visiting Tunisian Prime Minister Hamed Karoui and his Moroccan counterpart Abdellatif Filali on Friday announced the setting up of a foreign ministry commission aimed at harmonising their countries' policies.

Morocco's official news agency MAP said the two men took the decision after talks on ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation. The commission is to meet "every six months and when circumstances demand it", said a communique at the end of Karoui's visit.

The North African countries are members of the Arab Maghreb Union, along with Algeria, Libya and Mauritania, but efforts to give the group a role in European and international affairs have been hampered by differences between members.
On Thursday, King Hassan of Morocco conferred with Karoui on bilateral, regional and international issues.
Karoui, who arrived on Wednesday, also discussed the situation in the Maghreb and Middle East with Filali.
